summary: Attu Heliport (QGQ) serves the small settlement of Attu in western Greenland, a remote coastal community in the Qeqertalik municipality. Like many heliports across Greenland, it provides a vital lifeline for residents, connecting them to larger towns and essential services since the settlement lacks road links to other communities. The facility supports both passenger transport and supply operations in this Arctic environment.
faqs:
Q: Who operates flights to Attu Heliport?
A: Air Greenland typically operates helicopter services to remote Greenlandic settlements like Attu, using their fleet of Sikorsky S-61 and Airbus H225 helicopters.

Q: Are there fixed-wing flights available at Attu?
A: No, Attu is served exclusively by helicopter due to its small size and remote location; fixed-wing aircraft are not available at this facility.

Q: How is Attu Heliport used?
A: The heliport primarily transports passengers, mail, fresh food, and medical supplies between Attu and larger regional centers in western Greenland.

Q: Is Attu Heliport open year-round?
A: Helicopter services in Greenland generally operate year-round but schedules can be affected by severe Arctic weather conditions, including heavy snow and storms.
transport_tips: Heliport access in Greenland is typically arranged through Air Greenland, often as part of a multi-stop route connecting several small settlements. Travelers should book well in advance, as flight schedules in remote areas are limited and can be weather-dependent. There are no ground transportation options to or from the heliport; the settlement itself is small enough to traverse on foot.
local_tip: Pack motion sickness remedies even for short helicopter flights in Greenland—Arctic turbulence and wind conditions around coastal cliffs can make even brief hops surprisingly bumpy.
